// Part: room: butler's pantry (interior: service pantry and passage to the kitchen).
// A cooper's store: barrels along the west wall, a potted-shelf row, a work counter with cauldron, smoker and anvil at the
// south-east end (the focal piece, seen from the north door), and standing lanterns on the barrels and the counter.
// Inner air x52..60 z54..60, floor row y4. Lanes kept clear: north door (56,54), east doors (60,56..57), south doors (52..55,60).
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

const ORIGIN = [52, 4, 54];

const LEGEND = {
  B: ["barrel", { facing: "up", open: "false" }],
  S: ["chest", { facing: "south" }],
  P: "dark_oak_planks",
  C: "cauldron",
  K: ["smoker", { facing: "north" }],
  A: ["anvil", { facing: "east" }],
  T: "flower_pot",
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

// y4: floor-level furniture. Rows z54..z60, columns x52..x60.
const FLOOR = [
  "BBL...SS.", // z54: barrels on the west wall, a lantern on the floor, chest dresser at the north-east
  "B........", // z55: barrel, lantern on top
  "B........", // z56: barrel
  ".........", // z57: east-west lane
  ".....PPPP", // z58: work counter (focal), south-east
  ".....PPPP", // z59: counter, second course
  "........B", // z60: barrel at the south-east corner
];

// y5: things standing on the furniture's top faces.
const TOPS = [
  "T........", // z54: pot on a barrel
  "L........", // z55: standing lantern on a barrel (the room's light)
  "T........", // z56: pot on a barrel
  ".........",
  ".....C.KA", // z58: cauldron, smoker, anvil on the counter
  ".....L...", // z59: lantern on the counter
  "........T", // z60: pot on the corner barrel
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, ORIGIN, LEGEND, [FLOOR, TOPS]);
}

input.summary:
room: butler's pantry (parts/room-9.mjs) is written with its 16 floor and 8 top blocks, all in palette.json, but 0 are placed. Every write is refused because the shell's box() fills the room interior with air, and the lock counts air as owned.
The refusal is not fixable inside room-9: standalone it places 24 with 0 refused, and after parts/shell.mjs it places 0. I did not edit any module or bypass the lock. make.sh still writes build.nbt, but without the pantry's furniture.
left: REFUSED 24 writes not fixed. Cause: parts/shell.mjs box() calls fill([x0+1,3,z0+1],[x1-1,17,z1-1],"air"), which marks every interior cell as owned by the shell, so no room part can place anything there (room-9 alone: placed 24, refused 0; shell then room-9: placed 0, refused 24). The fix belongs to the shell's owner: drop that explicit air fill (a fresh grid is already air) or let runParts count air-over-air as unowned. Then re-run ./make.sh and confirm the pantry line shows placed 24.

OFF-PALETTE: none. Checked standalone (placed 24, offPalette []): barrel, chest, lantern, cauldron, smoker, anvil, flower_pot and dark_oak_planks are all in palette.json, so room-9 needs no block swaps.
build.nbt is written by make.sh, but the pantry's furniture is absent from it until the shell fix lands. This part is not finished.

waste.what: Finding why every write was refused meant running the part on its own and then after the shell, in a temp script, to compare placed and refused counts.
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the owning earlier part and the owner's write (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell: air fill'), and flag when a refused write is air-over-air, so the cause shows in the one make.sh line.

waste.what: The OFF-PALETTE check was hidden because the refused writes never reach the palette check, so I had to run the part alone to see its palette result.
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette report on every attempted write, including refused ones, so OFF-PALETTE is reported alongside REFUSED.

waste.what: Checking each legend id against palette.json by reading the file, role by role.
waste.tool: `$MCD blocks --check` over the part's LEGEND ids, or an off-palette list that runs before the lock check.

Once the pantry is unlocked, check the barrel facing and open states, the chest dresser, and the lanterns standing on the barrel and counter tops in room-9's layout.

structured_output.summary:
room: butler's pantry (parts/room-9.mjs) is written with its 16 floor and 8 top blocks, all in palette.json, but 0 are placed. Every write is refused because the shell's box() fills the room interior with air, and the lock counts air as owned.
The refusal is not fixable inside room-9: standalone it places 24 with 0 refused, and after parts/shell.mjs it places 0. I did not edit any module or bypass the lock. make.sh still writes build.nbt, but without the pantry's furniture.
left: REFUSED 24 writes not fixed. Cause: parts/shell.mjs box() calls fill([x0+1,3,z0+1],[x1-1,17,z1-1],"air"), which marks every interior cell as owned by the shell, so no room part can place anything there (room-9 alone: placed 24, refused 0; shell then room-9: placed 0, refused 24). The fix belongs to the shell's owner: drop that explicit air fill (a fresh grid is already air) or let runParts count air-over-air as unowned. Then re-run ./make.sh and confirm the pantry line shows placed 24.

OFF-PALETTE: none. Checked standalone (placed 24, offPalette []): barrel, chest, lantern, cauldron, smoker, anvil, flower_pot and dark_oak_planks are all in palette.json, so room-9 needs no block swaps.
build.nbt is written by make.sh, but the pantry's furniture is absent from it until the shell fix lands. This part is not finished.

waste.what: Finding why every write was refused meant running the part on its own and then after the shell, in a temp script, to compare placed and refused counts.
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the owning earlier part and the owner's write (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell: air fill'), and flag when a refused write is air-over-air, so the cause shows in the one make.sh line.

waste.what: The OFF-PALETTE check was hidden because the refused writes never reach the palette check, so I had to run the part alone to see its palette result.
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette report on every attempted write, including refused ones, so OFF-PALETTE is reported alongside REFUSED.

waste.what: Checking each legend id against palette.json by reading the file, role by role.
waste.tool: `$MCD blocks --check` over the part's LEGEND ids, or an off-palette list that runs before the lock check.

Once the pantry is unlocked, check the barrel facing and open states, the chest dresser, and the lanterns standing on the barrel and counter tops in room-9's layout.
